{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative bias (e.g., -0.25 or below) to counteract overconfidence in upward moves.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early stages of downward trends (e.g., after 3–5 consecutive negative sentiment entries) to avoid overcorrection.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.",
    "When sentiment shifts from neutral to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.50+), slightly increase forecast lag by 1–2 days to avoid premature spikes.",
    "After sharp price spikes (forecast >75% above prior peak), apply a 3–5 day cooling-off rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% per day until trend stabilizes.",
    "If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive underperformance), apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% to avoid overestimating upside.",
    "For sentiment history with 0.33+ positive bias, increase forecast sensitivity to recent price action (e.g., 2–3 day moving average) to avoid lagging behind momentum.",
    "When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending downward, apply a 3–5% downward bias to prevent overestimating recovery potential."
  ]
}
